About

A student from Sindh building technology that makes climate claims checkable.

The idea

What if a phone camera could help verify that a climate action really happened, and keep that proof on a blockchain?

No middleman, no self-reported data, no greenwashing. I called it GaiaVolt. You take a photo of a real green action, an AI model checks it, and the result is recorded on the Polygon blockchain. It started as a project named EcoX, and I renamed it GaiaVolt in June 2026.

I started on 7 May 2026, the day my last exam ended, and built the first working version in 35 days. I keep testing and improving it. The checks are meant to catch duplicate photos, photos in the wrong category, and random images from the internet. There is a lot left to learn, and that is the point.

What I care about

I’m proud to be from Sindh. Everything I’ve built so far, I built here.

I care about women in tech and AI. I know how rare it still is to see girls in these rooms, and I want to be one more voice, so that other girls from places like mine can see they belong in tech too.

What I want to do next

Many people in small villages don’t have easy access to technology or a stable internet connection. My next mission is to learn how to build AI that works offline, and to use my skills to help people in those villages.

It may start small: one village, one tool, one person at a time. I would rather start small than not start.

I’m also building a network of students, developers, researchers and people who care about the planet. If you’re working on something meaningful, I’d love to learn from you.

GaiaVolt: Proof of Planet

AI-powered environmental verification on blockchain

Solo build, 35 days. Founder and full-stack developer. Live MVP on Polygon testnet, still in active development.

GaiaVolt verifies real eco-actions using AI and seals the proof permanently on a blockchain. A user takes a photo of a sustainable action, like planting a tree, installing solar panels or recycling, and the system checks that it is real in under 10 seconds.

79.83%accuracy on a 238-image validation set
5 of 5internal fraud tests passed
35 dayssolo build to a first working version
32 GAIAtokens locked until 1 January 2050

The problem

Corporate sustainability claims are mostly self-reported and hard to verify. GaiaVolt aims to give companies tamper-proof, blockchain-anchored evidence for ESG reporting and supplier sustainability checks.

How it works

  1. 1Take a photoOf a real green action.
  2. 2AI checks itIn under 10 seconds.
  3. 3Proof is sealedStored on IPFS and recorded on Polygon.

The product

Fraud protection

  • GPS verification
  • Image fingerprinting to catch duplicate photos
  • Liveness detection
  • AI confidence threshold

It passed 5 of 5 of my internal fraud tests.

Features

  • QuantumLock 2050: a smart contract holding 32 GAIA tokens, locked until 1 January 2050
  • Gasless transactions using ERC-4337 account abstraction
  • Installable PWA, no app store needed
  • Carbon impact engine using the NASA POWER API and IPCC AR6 constants
  • Evolution system with 7 levels, from Seedling to Carbon Zero Hero
  • Dynamic NFTs for monthly top performers

Built with

  • AITensorFlow, EfficientNetB0, TFLite
  • BlockchainSolidity, Polygon, ERC-20 token (GAIA)
  • PrivacyZK-SNARKs with Circom and snarkjs, which I’m still learning
  • BackendPython, Flask, Docker, Gunicorn
  • FrontendNext.js, React, Three.js, Framer Motion
  • StorageIPFS with AES-256 encryption, Pinata
  • AuthSupabase, JWT
  • HostingHuggingFace Spaces (API), Vercel (frontend)

An idea I’m exploring

A B2B API subscription for sustainability managers who need verified supplier ESG data: $500 per year per company, for up to 100 verifications. This is a plan, not a running business yet.

Quetico Superior Resources Inc.

A website for a Canadian mineral exploration company. Client project. Web developer.

What it does

A professional website for a junior exploration company searching for gold, copper and platinum group metals in northwestern Ontario. It tells the company’s story and shows its exploration approach, its projects and its field programme to investors and the public.

  • Homepage with a sunrise hero image and the company’s story
  • Pages for About Us, Exploration, Projects, Field Programme, News and Contact
  • Contact form that delivers messages straight to the company’s email
  • Social sharing preview image and a layout that works on phones

Built with Next.js and deployed on Vercel. Contact emails are sent with Resend.

Aethrix

What it does

A curated place for artists, with no algorithms and no noise. Artists apply for an “Artist Passport” to join a creative community.

    Recognition

    The UN/ITU pitch, awards and the courses behind my work.

    The UN/ITU pitch

    On 6 October 2026 I presented GaiaVolt live at the AI for Climate Innovation Factory 2026 pitching session. It is part of the AI for Good Innovation Factory, run by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the United Nations agency for digital technologies.

    GaiaVolt uses AI to check photos of real climate actions and records the proof on a blockchain, so that climate claims can be verified instead of self-reported. That is what I took to the session.
